# Goban Studio v13.0.0

v13 keeps the four spaces of v12 and makes the app something you can rely
on: the count is right, your games and files are never lost or written
over, the desktop shell trusts the page less, problems are graded and
placed for people, review varies each problem and spaces it by memory, and
the course has new units from ko fighting to handicap Go. v13 reads
everything v9–v12 saved and moves it to the v13 format.

## Download and first launch

| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `GobanStudio-macOS-arm64.dmg` or `.zip` | See the package README. |
| macOS (Intel) | `GobanStudio-macOS-x64.dmg` or `.zip` | See the package README. |
| Windows (x64) | `GobanStudio-Windows-x64.zip` | See the package README. |
<!-- /first-launch -->

`SHA256SUMS` lists the checksums of every file. Windows on ARM runs the x64
build under the system's emulation.

## Correct results

- **Counting.** An area that touches all four sides of the board was always
  counted as neutral, even when one side had sealed the other's living
  group into a corner: a 9×9 game won by about 60 points could be scored
  for the loser. It is now territory whenever the other colour has a
  living group of its own, under Japanese, Chinese and Korean rules.
- **SGF.** Set-up stones in the second node are the starting position;
  stones added or removed during a game are applied before the next move
  (and exported back); GB2312/GBK, Big5, Shift_JIS, EUC-JP and EUC-KR files
  read correctly; a handicap given as moves is not placed twice; sizes
  other than 9, 13 and 19 are refused with a message instead of turning
  into 19×19; a bad point is a warning, not a silent pass; records of
  10,000 moves or 5,000 nested variations load.
- **Problems.** The solver no longer reuses results that depended on the
  order it searched in, and a search from a position on an answer line
  respects what that line already played. One problem gained a second
  correct answer that was always right; seki-01's answer line ends in seki
  again. A search cut short by its budget is "not proved", never "wrong".
- **The computer** never picks a move that repeats a position, and if
  KataGo gives no move, the offline engine plays one (or the panel offers
  Retry). A hint or a count that arrives after you undo is dropped.

## Nothing lost

- **A game in progress is never thrown away.** New game, "Play from here"
  and opening another game save it to the Library as unfinished; open it
  to continue where you left off. Unfinished games are never rated.
- **A file that can't be read is never written over.** If the settings,
  player model or current game can't be read at start, the app opens in a
  safe state (Retry, or continue read-only) instead of starting over as a
  new player; a damaged file is copied aside first.
- **Restoring a backup** first keeps a snapshot of what was there; Settings
  → Data can undo the last restore. Backups from v9–v12 are migrated.
- **Exports** that can't be written say so, instead of "Exported".
- **Quitting** waits briefly for the last changes to be saved.
- **Storage** is versioned with step-by-step migrations (`docs/storage.md`).
  Game files keep the analysis they need and load on demand: start-up
  reads three small files however many games you have.

## A narrower, safer shell

- The page can read and write only files you chose in the app's own open
  and save dialogs, opened with the app or dropped on it: `.sgf`, `.json`
  and `.png`.
- The development server address is no longer allowed in release builds.
- Builds are ReleaseSafe: an out-of-bounds access stops the app instead of
  corrupting memory.
- Every KataGo request has a deadline; a stuck KataGo is restarted and the
  request answered. The old synchronous KataGo calls are gone.
- **Updates** install only the version the last check found, and only if
  it is newer. The app quits for an update only after the update helper
  has shown that it started, and two helpers never run at once. Releases
  can carry an Ed25519 signature of `SHA256SUMS`, checked by builds made
  with the project's public key (`docs/signing.md`); this release is built
  without a key, so updates are still verified by checksum only.

## Practice that fits

- **Grades for people.** Problem grades now measure what a person must
  read — real branching, tempting wrong moves, the kind of problem —
  rather than how hard the solver worked. A plain ladder is grade 1, not
  grade 5 (`docs/problems-audit.md`, "v13 grading").
- **Placement** is 10–12 problems drawn for you, mixing capturing, escaping,
  living and killing; a grade counts only after two solves; it never places
  you above about 10 kyu until your own results say so.
- **Review** shows a problem you have seen before turned, mirrored or with
  the colours swapped, so you read it again instead of remembering where
  the answer was. When it comes back follows a memory model: intervals
  grow past three weeks, a miss shortens the interval instead of starting
  over, mastered problems retire, and at most 12 reviews come due a day.
- **Confirm moves in problems** (Settings → Playing): the first click shows
  the stone, the second plays it.
- **Your solving level** needs consistent results at the grades below too.
- **Your moves look like…** With KataGo's human model installed, the
  review estimates the rank your moves resemble, with its range.

## New in the course (23 units, 104 lessons)

- **Ko fighting** — threats, real and fake threats, counting threats,
  starting and ending a ko.
- **Judging the position** — counting in the middle game, playing safe when
  ahead, taking chances when behind.
- **Area scoring** — counting stones and territory (komi 7.5), and which
  rules your games use.
- **The endgame, rebuilt** on sealed, real positions: sente and gote,
  reverse sente, double sente, counting a move, big–middle–small, and why
  a big gote can beat a small double sente.
- **Openings** — the Chinese opening, sanrensei, the direction of play,
  urgent points before big points.
- **Joseki** — low and two-space pincers, the high approach, the knight's
  approach, choosing a joseki by the position.
- **Handicap Go** — for Black and for White.
- Fixes: a Lee Changho note (his first world title was the 1992 Tong-Yang
  Cup), the Game of the Century note, Korean and Chinese names in the
  classics, and consistent terms ("rabbity six"; Japanese 呼吸点 and
  カケツギ).

## Interface

- Play with no game on it shows its home: the suggested game, with its
  handicap, and New game.
- Small grey text now meets 4.5:1 contrast; Windows high-contrast mode is
  supported; dangerous confirmations focus Cancel.
- Counts read right in English ("1 move"), Chinese and Japanese get
  full-width colons, Korean particles follow the word; a missing string
  falls back to English.
- A timed game no longer redraws the whole window four times a second; the
  start-up script is a third smaller.

## Engineering

- Pull requests now build and test the native shell; the release tag is
  bound to the commit that was built and to the app's version; every
  downloaded binary and the bundled network are pinned by SHA-256; actions
  are pinned by commit; tokens are read-only except where a job publishes.
- New `SECURITY.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`; `docs/QA.md` rewritten.

## Known limits

- **Not checked by people.** No usability test, no strong player's review
  of the new lessons (the steps most in need are listed in
  `docs/lesson-audit.md`), no native-speaker review of the Chinese, Korean
  and Japanese text, and no real screen-reader session.
- **The KataGo audit of the new lessons has not run yet.** Their
  interactive steps are proved by the solver; the place steps and the
  claims in read steps wait for the next `lesson-check` run.
- The builds are not code-signed, and this release carries no update
  signature (no key is configured yet).
- Holding quit until the page has saved is implemented for macOS and
  Windows but has not been tried on a real Mac or PC; if it does not work
  there, the app quits after 1.5–3 seconds as before.
- "Your moves look like…" and the native human-policy command were tested
  against recorded KataGo output, not a live KataGo.
- If every stone of one side is marked dead, the open board is still
  counted as neutral, as before.
- The counting solver ignores ko threats; endgame problems avoid ko.
